chunks: Ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Ali, from his father, from al-Rayyan, from al-Ridha, from his forefathers, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, said: He has not believed in Me the one who interprets My words by his opinion. He has not known Me the one who likens Me to My creatures. He is not upon My religion the one who uses analogy in My religion.
ai.seo_question: What are the three signs of true belief in God according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi, transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt chain, underscores the Shia principle of tanzih (divine transcendence) by critiquing anthropomorphism (tashbih) and the over-reliance on human analogical reasoning (qiyas) in theology. It highlights that true gnosis of God requires moving beyond subjective interpretation and physical likeness to recognize His unique essence, a core tenet in Shia usul al-din.

en.ammaar-muslim: 6. [6/334] al-Tawhid, al-Uyun and al-Amali: Ibn al-Mutawakkil from Ali from his father from al-Rayyan from al-Ridha from his forefathers from The Commander of the Faithful عليهم السلام who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه واله said: Allah Majestic is His Majesty said: He has not believed in Me the one who interprets My words by his opinion. He has not known Me the one who likens Me to My creatures. He is not upon My religion the one who uses analogy in My religion.
